name: Ahaziah of Judah
charge: Walking in the ways of the house of Ahab, his mother being his counsellor to do wickedly
summary: Ahaziah followed the counsel of his mother and Ahab's house. He joined Joram in war and visited him at Jezreel. His coming to Joram brought him into the judgment executed by Jehu. He was killed, and those who buried him remembered the faithfulness of his forefather Jehoshaphat.
offense: Ahaziah followed the counsel of his mother and the house of Ahab. Those who should have guided the young king toward the Lord became his counselors to his destruction. He joined Joram of Israel in war against Hazael and afterward went to visit the wounded king at Jezreel. His connection to Jehoshaphat did not make his own conduct righteous. He chose the ways of Ahab's house and joined its cause when judgment was approaching it.
judgment: Chronicles declares that Ahaziah's destruction was of God in coming to Joram. He went out with him against Jehu, whom the Lord had anointed to cut off Ahab's house. Jehu's men also killed the princes of Judah and Ahaziah's relatives who attended him. Ahaziah was sought out and killed. Those who buried him remembered Jehoshaphat, his forefather, who had sought the Lord with all his heart. That remembered faithfulness secured a measure of regard at his burial, but it had not sheltered Ahaziah from the consequences of his own alliance. His house was left without strength to retain the kingdom.

verses.text: And the inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah his youngest son king in his stead: for the band of men that came with the Arabians to the camp had slain all the eldest. So Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah reigned.
Forty and two years old was Ahaziah when he began to reign, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother’s name also was Athaliah the daughter of Omri.
He also walked in the ways of the house of Ahab: for his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly.
Wherefore he did evil in the sight of the Lord like the house of Ahab: for they were his counsellors after the death of his father to his destruction.
He walked also after their counsel, and went with Jehoram the son of Ahab king of Israel to war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth–gilead: and the Syrians smote Joram.

And he returned to be healed in Jezreel because of the wounds which were given him at Ramah, when he fought with Hazael king of Syria. And Azariah the son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Jehoram the son of Ahab at Jezreel, because he was sick.
And the destruction of Ahaziah was of God by coming to Joram: for when he was come, he went out with Jehoram against Jehu the son of Nimshi, whom the Lord had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab.
And it came to pass, that, when Jehu was executing judgment upon the house of Ahab, and found the princes of Judah, and the sons of the brethren of Ahaziah, that ministered to Ahaziah, he slew them.

And he sought Ahaziah: and they caught him, (for he was hid in Samaria,) and brought him to Jehu: and when they had slain him, they buried him: Because, said they, he is the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the Lord with all his heart. So the house of Ahaziah had no power to keep still the kingdom.
In the twelfth year of Joram the son of Ahab king of Israel did Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah begin to reign.
Two and twenty years old was Ahaziah when he began to reign; and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Athaliah, the daughter of Omri king of Israel.
And he walked in the way of the house of Ahab, and did evil in the sight of the Lord, as did the house of Ahab: for he was the son in law of the house of Ahab.
And he went with Joram the son of Ahab to the war against Hazael king of Syria in Ramoth–gilead; and the Syrians wounded Joram.

And king Joram went back to be healed in Jezreel of the wounds which the Syrians had given him at Ramah, when he fought against Hazael king of Syria. And Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Joram the son of Ahab in Jezreel, because he was sick.

But when Ahaziah the king of Judah saw this, he fled by the way of the garden house. And Jehu followed after him, and said, Smite him also in the chariot. And they did so at the going up to Gur, which is by Ibleam. And he fled to Megiddo, and died there.
And his servants carried him in a chariot to Jerusalem, and buried him in his sepulchre with his fathers in the city of David.
And in the eleventh year of Joram the son of Ahab began Ahaziah to reign over Judah.
He that walketh with wise men shall be wise: but a companion of fools shall be destroyed.

entries.commentary: The inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah, Jehoram's youngest son, king in his stead, for the band of Arabians had slain all the elder sons. Ahaziah was forty and two years old when he began to reign and reigned one year in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Athaliah the daughter of Omri. He walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly, and the house of Ahab were his counsellors after his father died, to his destruction. This is a warning against being ruled by the wrong counsel: instead of going to the priests and the judges, he went to his mother, and she counselled him into ruin. A woman with a grudge can rule a kingdom through her son, and that is what Athaliah did.

Ahaziah walked after their counsel and went with Jehoram son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth-gilead, where Jehoram was wounded. He went down to see the wounded Jehoram at Jezreel, and the destruction of Ahaziah was of the Most High, for by going he came into the path of Jehu, whom the Most High had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab. That same Jehu who killed the seventy sons of Ahab found the princes of Judah and the sons of Ahaziah's brethren and slew them, then sought and caught Ahaziah, who was hid in Samaria. They buried Ahaziah for the sake of Jehoshaphat his forefather who sought the Most High with all his heart; but the house of Ahaziah had no power to keep the kingdom, so the wicked king was cut off by the same hand the Most High anointed to avenge Israel.

When Athaliah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the seed royal of the house of Judah, killing the king's sons. But Jehoshabeath the daughter of king Jehoram, wife of Jehoiada the priest and sister of Ahaziah, took Joash the son of Ahaziah and stole him from among the king's sons that were slain, hiding him and his nurse in a bedchamber. She hid the child in the house of God six years while Athaliah reigned over the land, showing that Athaliah was ruling in the position of the son she had lost. Athaliah did not carry out this slaughter alone; she had weak men helping her run over everything, which is how she seized and held the throne.

Elisha warns the Shunammite woman whose son he restored to flee the coming seven year famine, and she sojourns in the land of the Philistines. When she returns to appeal to the king for her house and land, Gehazi is at that moment telling the king how Elisha restored a dead body to life. The timing is of the Most High, so the king restores all that was hers and the fruits of the field from the day she left.

Ben-hadad king of Syria, sick, sends Hazael to inquire of Elisha whether he will recover, for the word of a prophet, also called a seer, was precious in those days. Elisha tells Hazael the king may recover but the Most High has shown that he shall surely die, then weeps because he sees the evil Hazael will do to Israel: burning strongholds, slaying young men, and ripping up women with child. Elisha tells Hazael he will be king over Syria, revealing that leadership can discern spirits at work in a man that the man does not see in himself. Hazael returns and smothers the king with a wet cloth and reigns in his place.

Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat begins to reign over Judah and walks in the way of the kings of Israel because the daughter of Ahab was his wife. He does evil in the sight of the Most High, yet Judah is not destroyed for David his servant's sake, according to the promise.

In Jehoram's days Edom revolts from under the hand of Judah and makes a king over itself, breaking the subjection Edom had been under from the days of David and Solomon. This revolt fulfills the word spoken to Esau, that when he gained the dominion he would break the yoke from off his neck, a pattern reaching to Edom's later rise. Jehoram sleeps with his fathers and is buried in the city of David, and Ahaziah his son reigns in his place. -

Ahaziah son of Jehoram begins to reign over Judah and walks in the way of the house of Ahab, being the son-in-law of that house, a picture of the generational curse passed from father to son. He goes with Jehoram son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Syria, and the Syrians wound Jehoram at Ramah. Jehoram returns to Jezreel to be healed, and Ahaziah goes down to see him, setting the stage for both kings to meet Jehu's judgment.

Elisha sends one of the children of the prophets to Ramoth-gilead to anoint Jehu king over Israel, pour the oil on his head, and flee. Jehu is charged to smite the house of Ahab to avenge the blood of the prophets and of the servants of the Most High shed at the hand of Jezebel, whose work was to kill the prophets while weak Ahab let it continue. The word declares the whole house of Ahab shall perish, and the dogs shall eat Jezebel in the portion of Jezreel with none to bury her.

Jehu's fellow captains ask why the mad fellow came, and when he tells them the prophet anointed him king, they hasten to put their garments under him and blow the trumpets, proclaiming Jehu king. Jehu conspires against Jehoram and charges that none escape the city to carry the news to Jezreel. He rides toward Jezreel where Jehoram lay wounded, and Ahaziah king of Judah had come down to see him.

A watchman spies Jehu's company, and two horsemen sent to ask if it is peace are each told to turn behind him and do not return, for the driving is furious like the driving of Jehu. Jehoram himself goes out and asks if it is peace, and Jehu answers that there can be no peace while the whoredoms and witchcrafts of his mother Jezebel are so many. Jehu draws his bow with full strength and smites Jehoram through the heart, then casts him into the portion of Naboth the Jezreelite according to the word of the Most High.

Ahaziah king of Judah flees but Jehu pursues and has him smitten in his chariot; he flees to Megiddo and dies there. His servants carry him to Jerusalem and bury him in the sepulchre of his fathers in the city of David.

Jezebel paints her face and tires her head, returning to her seductive ways as Jehu enters the gate. Jehu calls out for who is on his side, and two or three eunuchs look out. At Jehu's word they throw her down, her blood is sprinkled on the wall and the horses, and he treads her under foot. When they go to bury her they find only the skull, the feet, and the palms of her hands, fulfilling the word spoken by Elijah that dogs would eat the flesh of Jezebel and her carcass would be as dung upon the field.

A wise son takes his father's instruction, but a scorner will not even hear rebuke. What you do with correction marks whether you are wise or a scorner. The scriptures constantly tell you to watch your mouth. Everything you say you will give account for, so he that guards his mouth keeps his life while the one who opens his lips wide brings destruction.

The lazy soul desires and has nothing, but the diligent soul is made fat. Desire without labor stays empty. The righteous man hates lying, but the wicked is loathsome and comes to shame. Righteousness keeps the upright, while wickedness overthrows the sinner.

Some make themselves rich yet have nothing, and some make themselves poor yet have great riches. This is the man who forsakes things when he comes into the truth, giving up sponsorships and possessions, yet he still has great riches because the kingdom of heaven is coming to him. A man's riches may be the ransom of his life, but the poor does not even hear rebuke.

The light of the righteous rejoices, but the lamp of the wicked is put out. Only by pride comes contention, but with the well-advised is wisdom, which points to seeking counsel at all times. Wealth gotten by vanity is diminished, but he that gathers by labor increases. Those chasing the fast dollar and fast money will see all those riches diminish.

Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but when the desire comes it is a tree of life. Whoever despises the word is destroyed, but he that fears the commandment is rewarded. The law of the wise is a fountain of life to depart from the snares of death.

Good understanding gives favor, but the way of transgressors is hard. Every prudent man deals with knowledge, but a fool lays his folly open for all to see. A wicked messenger falls into mischief, but a faithful ambassador is health.

Poverty and shame come to the one who refuses instruction, but he that regards reproof is honored. He that walks with wise men shall be wise, but a companion of fools is destroyed. Every beast cleaves to its like: around fools you become a fool, around wise men you become wise.

Evil pursues sinners, but the righteous are repaid with good. A good man leaves an inheritance to his children's children, and the wealth of the sinner is laid up for the just. This is powerful for us as a nation. A lot of black people do not like to talk about death, but get your life insurance and leave an inheritance to your children's children. That is how far ahead we have to think.

He that spares his rod hates his son, but he that loves him disciplines him early. Discipline your children. Esau has set it up so no one wants anyone to discipline our kids, but the discipline is a bullet. The righteous eats to the satisfying of his soul, but the belly of the wicked shall want.
